new_task_1.title: Refresh stale system time warning cutoff
new_task_1.description: urllib3 2.5.0 refreshes the RECENT_DATE cutoff used by connection-time stale clock checks from 2023-06-01 to 2025-01-01, so more outdated local system dates are treated as suspicious.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure urllib3's connection-layer stale system time detection uses a current recent-date threshold rather than an obsolete 2023 cutoff.

expectation.grounded: urllib3.connection.RECENT_DATE must be set to datetime.date(2025, 1, 1) instead of datetime.date(2023, 6, 1). Code paths that compare the current date against RECENT_DATE should therefore classify dates before 2025-01-01 according to the existing stale-time behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Users with a significantly outdated system clock should receive urllib3's existing stale-time signal based on a threshold appropriate for the 2.5.0 release timeframe.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the warning class, warning message semantics, connection establishment behavior, or TLS configuration behavior beyond the updated RECENT_DATE cutoff. Do not treat the package version bump as part of this behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be limited to refreshing the age threshold used by the existing clock sanity check.

behavior: The stale system time cutoff in urllib3.connection is 2025-01-01.
Dates before 2025-01-01 now fall below the recent-date threshold used by urllib3's existing stale-time check.
Dates from 2023-06-01 through 2024-12-31, which were not below the previous threshold, are now considered stale by the refreshed cutoff.
Existing connection, warning, and TLS behavior outside the cutoff comparison remains unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Given urllib3.connection is imported, when RECENT_DATE is inspected, then it should equal datetime.date(2025, 1, 1).
Given the existing stale-time check compares the current date to RECENT_DATE, when the current date is 2024-12-31, then it should follow the stale-time path associated with dates before RECENT_DATE.
Given the current date is on or after 2025-01-01, when the existing stale-time check runs, then the refreshed cutoff alone should not classify that date as stale.
When connections are created under normal system dates, urllib3 should preserve the existing connection and TLS behavior apart from the updated clock cutoff.

new_task_2.title: Update deprecated API removal warnings
new_task_2.description: urllib3 2.5.0 updates runtime deprecation warnings for HTTPResponse.getheaders(), HTTPResponse.getheader(), and the ssl_version option to state that removal is planned for urllib3 v2.6.0 instead of v2.1.0.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure user-facing deprecation warnings communicate the current planned removal version for APIs that remain present in urllib3 2.5.0.

expectation.grounded: BaseHTTPResponse.getheaders(), BaseHTTPResponse.getheader(), and urllib3.util.ssl_.create_urllib3_context when called with ssl_version must emit DeprecationWarning messages that say removal will occur in urllib3 v2.6.0. The existing replacement guidance for each deprecated API must remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: Callers should receive accurate deprecation timeline information at runtime without any functional change to the deprecated APIs before their removal.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove getheaders(), getheader(), or ssl_version support in this change. Do not change the warning category, stacklevel, replacement guidance, return values, header lookup behavior, or SSL context creation behavior beyond the removal-version text.
constraints.conceptual: The change should correct public lifecycle messaging while preserving compatibility for callers still using the deprecated APIs.

behavior: Calling HTTPResponse.getheaders() continues to emit a DeprecationWarning, but the warning now names urllib3 v2.6.0 as the removal version.
Calling HTTPResponse.getheader(name, default) continues to emit a DeprecationWarning, but the warning now names urllib3 v2.6.0 as the removal version.
Calling create_urllib3_context with the deprecated ssl_version option continues to emit a DeprecationWarning, but the warning now names urllib3 v2.6.0 as the removal version.
The recommended replacements remain HTTPResponse.headers, HTTPResponse.headers.get(name, default), and ssl_minimum_version respectively.
The deprecated APIs continue to perform their existing behavior after emitting the updated warnings.
acceptance_criteria: Given a response object, when HTTPResponse.getheaders() is called, then a DeprecationWarning should mention removal in urllib3 v2.6.0 and direct callers to HTTPResponse.headers.

Given a response object, when HTTPResponse.getheader(name, default) is called, then a DeprecationWarning should mention removal in urllib3 v2.6.0 and direct callers to HTTPResponse.headers.get(name, default).
Given create_urllib3_context is called with ssl_version, then a DeprecationWarning should mention removal in urllib3 v2.6.0 and direct callers to ssl_minimum_version.
When these deprecated APIs are called, their warning category should remain DeprecationWarning and their existing runtime behavior should remain unchanged apart from the updated message text.
